docs.title: Sankhara
docs.text:
Sankhara is a turn-based world game played on a procedurally generated hex map. You are born into a family on a tile of the world, act each turn, and those actions shape your health and karma — and, eventually, what you are reborn as.

The name comes from the Pali saṅkhāra: the mental formations and volitional impulses that, in Buddhist thought, condition what comes next. See Concepts.

Status

Early prototype. Map generation, resources, a basic player/family model and turn actions exist; karma, NPCs and terrain are still stubs.

docs.title: Running
docs.text:
uv sync
uv run sankhara        # or: uv run python -m sankhara

From the main menu choose New Game, click a tile to inspect it, and use the info panel to start a life and take actions.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
All code lives in the sankhara package under src/.

Package Responsibility sankhara.constants config.py: every tunable value — noise parameters, map size, biome thresholds and resource baselines, hex geometry, player actions, culture groups. sankhara.world Map generation (map_gen.py) and resource extraction/regeneration (resources.py). sankhara.core game_engine.generate_map() builds the map; turn_manager applies end-of-turn resource regeneration and action effects. sankhara.entities Player, PlayerState, Family (lineage) and name generation. sankhara.ui Kivy widgets: the info/action panel (ui_kivy.py) and screens (menu, map view, game over). sankhara.app SankharaApp and the screen manager wiring; main() is the entry point.

docs.title: World generation
docs.text:
1. Perlin noise (noise library) produces elevation and moisture grids of MAP_WIDTH × MAP_HEIGHT, normalised to [0, 1].
  2. Each value is bucketed by ELEVATION_THRESHOLDS / MOISTURE_THRESHOLDS; the pair names the biome (e.g. "Hill Forest").
  3. Resources are seeded from BIOME_RESOURCE_BASELINES with ± RESOURCE_VARIATION_PERCENTAGE random variation.

The map is a list of columns of tile dicts with id, q, r (axial hex coordinates), elevation, moisture, biome, abbr and resources.

docs.title: Turn loop
docs.text: At the end of a turn process_player_actions() adds each taken action's karma and health effects, applies skip penalties for skippable actions not taken, and clamps karma to [-1, 1] and health to [0, 100]. regenerate_resources() then regrows renewable resources toward their biome maximum.

docs.title: Stubs
docs.text: core/karma.py, entities/npc.py, world/terrain.py and world/biomes.py are empty placeholders for planned features.

docs.title: Concepts
docs.text: The game's mechanics are meant to model a handful of Buddhist ideas. This page is a skeleton to be expanded from the original design conversation.

docs.title: Saṅkhāra
docs.text: Mental formations or volitional impulses: one of the five aggregates and the second link of dependent origination. In the game, the accumulated effect of a character's choices.

docs.title: Karma
docs.text: Intentional action and its consequences. Each turn's actions (and skipped obligations) adjust a karma score clamped to [-1, 1]; see ACTIONS in sankhara/constants/config.py.

docs.title: Rebirth and lineage
docs.text: A player is born into a Family on a home tile, which determines their culture group and names. Player.reincarnate() swaps in a new state (and optionally a new family); how karma drives rebirth is still to be designed.

docs.title: Open questions
docs.text:
• How karma maps to the next birth (species, family, location).
  • Whether NPCs share the same karma model.

docs.title: Development
docs.text:
Requires uv. The project is pinned to Python 3.12 (.python-version); uv will download it if needed.

uv sync                     # create .venv with runtime + dev dependencies
uv run pre-commit install   # run ruff and basic checks on every commit

docs.title: Common commands
docs.text: Task Command Run the game uv run sankhara Tests (with coverage) uv run pytest Lint uv run ruff check . Format uv run ruff format . All pre-commit hooks uv run pre-commit run --all-files Docs preview uv run --group docs mkdocs serve

docs.title: Tests
docs.text: Tests live in tests/, mirroring the package layout (test_core/, test_world/, …). tests/conftest.py sets KIVY_NO_ARGS so Kivy doesn't consume pytest's arguments. UI tests need a display; CI runs them under xvfb-run.

docs.title: CI
docs.text: GitHub Actions runs lint and tests on every push and pull request (.github/workflows/ci.yml), and publishes these docs to GitHub Pages on pushes to main (.github/workflows/docs.yml).
